hook.text: Camels and llamas make antibodies with no light chains — just a single heavy chain. They are tiny and tough.

buildup.text: The antigen-binding domain is just 15 kDa — one-tenth the size of a regular antibody. It is called a nanobody.

discovery.text: Nanobodies penetrate tissues that full antibodies cannot reach — including solid tumors and the blood-brain barrier.

twist.text: They survive boiling and stomach acid — opening the door to oral and inhaled biologic drugs.

climax.text: Cablivi, the first approved nanobody, treats blood clotting disorders — camelid biology becomes human medicine.

punchline.text: From llama blood to human drugs — nanobodies are small but mighty.

quiz.question: What makes nanobodies different from conventional antibodies?
options: They are synthetic chemicals, not proteins
They are ten times smaller, more stable, and derived from camelid heavy-chain-only antibodies
They can only be used in veterinary medicine

details.summary: Nanobodies are antibody fragments derived from camelid heavy-chain antibodies that are one-tenth the size of conventional antibodies. Their small size enables them to reach hidden epitopes, cross the blood-brain barrier, and be produced cheaply in microorganisms.
details.whyItMatters: Nanobodies combine the specificity of antibodies with the advantages of small molecules. Their unique properties enable applications in brain diseases, diagnostics, and industrial settings that are impossible with conventional antibodies.
takeaways: Nanobodies come from camelid antibodies that lack light chains naturally
They are one-tenth the size of conventional antibodies at only 15 kDa
Caplacizumab was the first approved nanobody drug in 2018

faq.question: Why do camels make special antibodies?
faq.answer: Camels, llamas, and alpacas naturally produce heavy-chain-only antibodies missing the light chain found in human antibodies. Their antigen-binding domain is a single small protein that folds and functions independently, making it ideal as a modular therapeutic building block.

faq.question: What advantages do nanobodies have for imaging and diagnostics?
faq.answer: Their tiny size means nanobodies clear from blood quickly, creating high-contrast images within hours rather than days. They penetrate tissues deeply, resist extreme pH and temperature, and can be linked into multispecific formats easily. This makes them ideal for rapid point-of-care diagnostics.
